Muse's bundled `plan` skill has an explicit Approval Gate (prose-only, no tool call) that live-drove to a real waiting-shaped turn end; the daemon's existing PendingWaitingCue prose heuristic caught the real captured closing line when run through the actual parser this session.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Does muse have a plan mode at all

Yes, and it is a genuinely distinct feature from both 2.17 (plain trailing-? question) and 2.19/wave-1's tool-permission approval flow (`kind:"approval"`, `decision_source.kind`). `muse skills inspect plan --json` (run live this session against the installed `muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`) shows a **bundled** (ships by default, `enabledDefault: true`) skill `bundled:plan`: "Create a grounded, decision-complete plan, then stop for approval... invoked via `/skill plan` or an explicit plan request." Extracting the full skill body from the live binary (`strings ~/.local/bin/muse`) surfaces its `## Approval Gate` section verbatim:
- "Present the complete reviewable Markdown plan exactly once in a normal user-visible assistant reply before asking for approval."
- "Do not call `request_user_input` for final plan approval. That tool remains reserved for necessary pre-draft user-owned choices."
- "After the canonical plan and any saved path, ask the user in prose to reply `Approve`, `Request changes`, or `Cancel`."
- "Stop after asking; do not start implementation until the user explicitly approves."

This is a real, deliberately-engineered stop-and-wait gate matching the scenario's process (agent emits a plan, pauses, user approves, work resumes) — not a repurposing of 2.17's or 2.19's mechanism. It differs from Claude Code's ExitPlanMode in one load-bearing way the skill text states explicitly: "Treat this as planning guidance, not a host-enforced mode. Do not claim that the host is blocking write tools, commands, edits, or approvals for you." There is no protocol-level tool (no `exit_plan_mode`-shaped call; `muse schema generate-json-schema`'s method index and a full-binary `strings` scan for `exit_plan`/`ExitPlan`/`plan_approval` all come up empty) and no `kind:"approval"` record — the gate is enforced purely by the model choosing to stop, per the skill's instructions, exactly as its own text says.

## Live probe (this session)

Ran `muse exec --trust-workspace "Plan how to add a one-line README.md file (just the word hello) to this empty directory. Use the plan skill."` against a fresh empty workspace. The skill fired for real (2 research subagents spawned and closed, `skill_read_observed`/`skill_reminder_decision` events present), the model produced a full canonical Markdown plan, and the turn's only top-level `assistant_message_committed` (the primary session made ZERO tool calls itself — all discovery was delegated) ends: "No plan file was created; this plan is inline only. Please reply `Approve`, `Request changes`, or `Cancel` — I will not implement until you explicitly approve." Immediately followed by `{"kind":"terminal","terminal":"completed"}` with no open tool call. Muse's OWN internal reminder agents independently characterize this as a stop-for-approval outcome (`goal-reminder`'s `reminder_proposal.decision_reason`: "Plan deliverable present and agent handed control to user for approval (Approve/Request changes/Cancel) with no later user message; task done per plan-skill stop-for-approval"; `verify-reminder` similarly: "agent produced inline plan and correctly stopped for approval"). Captured transcript: `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/95bcac9d-baf7-46bb-8811-fb0e2412dfbc/session.jsonl`.

## Daemon

No tool call is open at turn end, so `NeedsUserAttention()`/`isUserBlockingTool` never applies here (this is NOT the request_user_input path muse's 2.17 cell uses) — the only candidate signal is the prose-cue heuristic already used by every other agent's plain-question cells: `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `parseAssistantMessageCommitted` sets `ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text))`. I did not stop at reading the wiring: I fed the REAL captured closing line from the live probe above through the actual `(&Parser{}).ParseLine` this session (a throwaway `_test.go`, removed afterward, not committed) and confirmed `EventType="assistant_message"`, `PendingWaitingCue=true`, `Skip=false`. The match comes from `waiting_cue.go`'s bucket-D curated-imperative pattern `\b(?:please|kindly)\s+\w+\b` on "Please reply" — a broad, high-recall pattern, not a narrow coincidence. `parser.go`'s `parseRunTerminal` sets `EventType="turn_done"` on the immediately-following `terminal:"completed"` record, so `SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone()` goes true with no open tool call and the classifier ladder (`NeedsUserAttention` → `OpenToolStalled` → `IsAgentDone` → `classifyAgentDone` → `IsWaitingForUserInput`) reaches `waiting` via `PendingWaitingCue`, exactly as it does for 2.17. No `kind:"approval"` record appears anywhere in the probe transcript (confirmed via a full payload-kind census of the session), so this is genuinely the prose path, not 2.19's tool-permission path — the two remain distinct even though both ultimately resolve to `waiting`.

The waiting→working→ready resume leg after an "Approve" reply was not separately live-probed: it is the ordinary same-session-id turn-resume mechanism every other multi-turn muse cell (2-1 basic-turn, 2-17, 2-19) already exercises, and the scenario's own canonical description explicitly scopes the recipe to entry only: "Recipe captures only entry into waiting; the approve/reject continuation is structurally identical to other waiting-resume paths" (also the exact convention claudecode's own already-recorded 2-18 cell follows: 3 phases, session_birth/turn_start/plan_mode_waiting, no resume phase).

## Driver

`send`/`wait_turn`/`sleep` are already implemented in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` (`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session"`), proven end-to-end for muse in the 2.17 cell's own record pass. No new primitive is needed for this recipe. No driver gap.

## Why this is not 2.17 or 2.19/wave-1's human_approval flow reused

- 2.17 (`user-blocking-question`) is a bare clarifying question with no plan artifact and an explicit "do not call any tools" instruction; its own metadata.json states it is "NOT the permission/approval-prompt scenario" and cites this cell (2.18) as the sibling that covers plan-mode. This assessment exercises the actual bundled `plan` skill and its dedicated Approval Gate section — a different, independently-triggered agent feature — not a copy of 2.17's recipe with different wording.
- Wave-1's `human_approval` finding (`--approval-judge off --approval-mode on-request` → `decision_source.kind:"human_approval"`) is muse's TOOL-permission gate (`kind:"approval"`) — it fires when a MUTATING tool call needs a human decision. The plan skill's Approval Gate is a distinct, earlier checkpoint that exists specifically to avoid ever reaching that tool-permission gate (the skill forbids mutating tool calls until the plan is approved). Neither the live probe's transcript nor the skill body reference `kind:"approval"` or the approval-judge/approval-mode settings at all — this cell's recipe does not depend on those settings, unlike 2.19.
caveats: Vacuous-pass rule: the exact closing sentence is model-generated free text, not a fixed template — the skill only mandates the CONTENT (ask to reply Approve/Request changes/Cancel) not the wording. This probe's phrasing ("Please reply...") hit waiting_cue.go's broad bucket-D `please + word` pattern, but a differently-worded run (e.g. a bare imperative list with no question mark and no cue word) could in principle land on neither ExtractQuestionSnippet nor ExtractWaitingCue and silently read as a stuck-working/ready session instead of waiting. This is a load-bearing agent-behaviour property, not a daemon defect — record should re-probe live and file an observability_correction if a differently-phrased run misses the cue.

The waiting→working→ready resume leg (after an "Approve" reply) was not live-probed in this assessment — only entry into waiting was driven, matching the scenario's own canonical scope ("Recipe captures only entry into waiting") and claudecode's already-recorded sibling cell for the same scenario.

This cell's recipe does NOT depend on --approval-mode/--approval-judge (unlike 2.19/tool-gate-permission-prompt and the wave-1 human_approval finding) — the plan skill's Approval Gate is a prose-only checkpoint that never reaches muse's tool-permission machinery. Re-probing on a host with different approval defaults should not change this cell's behaviour, but is untested.

Muse spawns ambient research/reminder subagents even for a pure planning request (2 children in this probe: a research child and the goal/verify reminder machinery) — the recipe's spec must pin every phase to the PRIMARY session (same_session_as) so a subagent's own ready/working transition can't silently satisfy an assertion, per the fleet-wide known contamination pattern for this adapter.

Grounded in a live probe run THIS session plus a throwaway parser unit-test run against the real captured text, but not yet a recorded, `of record`-verified fixture; record is what promotes it from provisional to settled.
